topics.topic: Whether the outer process bound is enforced by the parent outside the sandbox or set by the runner inside it
questions: Must the parent enforce the process bound from outside, or must the runner set that outer bound inside the sandbox?
Must the outer process bound be enforced by the parent from outside, or set by the runner inside the sandbox?
Must the process bound be enforced by the parent from outside, or set by the runner inside the sandbox?

quotes: The parent MUST enforce bounds from outside
the outer process bound is the setrlimit limit on the number of processes at bounds.process_count + 1, set by the runner inside the sandbox's user namespace before it loads the code
judgement.why: The first passage assigns outside enforcement to the parent, while the second assigns the outer process limit to the runner inside the sandbox.

topics.topic: How bubblewrap preserves the inherited trap-channel descriptor for the runner without a descriptor-preservation option
questions: How must bubblewrap preserve these descriptors for its child if the option required to preserve inherited descriptors is declared not to exist?

The runner must inherit the trap-channel descriptor, but subprocess pass_fds carries it only into bubblewrap; if bubblewrap has no descriptor-preservation option, how can bubblewrap be required to keep that descriptor open for the runner?

quotes: Every descriptor the environment needs from the parent — the write end of the trap channel, the --info-fd pipe — reaches bubblewrap by inheritance, passed with subprocess pass_fds, and bubblewrap keeps it open for the child: bubblewrap has no option that names a descriptor to keep, and --preserve-fds does not exist.
judgement.why: The text explicitly requires pass_fds inheritance into bubblewrap and requires bubblewrap to keep the descriptors open for its child.

topics.topic: Whether the launch environment is strictly SANDBOX_ENVIRONMENT or may temporarily include PWD and a locale variable
questions: Must the environment never receive variables outside SANDBOX_ENVIRONMENT, or may it temporarily receive PWD and a locale variable before the runner clears them?
Is the launch environment exactly SANDBOX_ENVIRONMENT, or does it also contain PWD and a locale variable until the runner resets it?
Must the environment never receive variables outside SANDBOX_ENVIRONMENT, or may PWD and a locale variable exist until the runner clears them?

quotes: Agent code is untrusted: it MUST only ever run inside a fresh bubblewrap environment created for that one execution, never in the kernel process and never through a faster path, and the environment never receives a credential, a host path other than its own exchange directory and the read-only runtime the next note binds (A03 rule 1, decision 25), or any variable outside the imported SANDBOX_ENVIRONMENT constant.
bubblewrap adds PWD after --clearenv and the interpreter's C-locale coercion adds a locale variable, so clearing at launch alone leaves both
judgement.why: One passage forbids the environment from ever receiving any extra variable, while the other says it receives PWD and a locale variable before the runner clears them.

topics.topic: Whether the scratch bound applies to the aggregate exchange directory or each individual file
questions: Must the constant bound the aggregate exchange directory, or only each individual file written there?

quotes: one fresh private exchange directory bound read-write and bounded by the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SANDBOX_SCRATCH_BYTES_MAX constant
the size of a file written in the scratch with setrlimit
judgement.why: The first passage bounds the exchange directory as a whole, while the second specifies a per-file size limit.

topics.topic: Returned activation value for a new refused verdict
questions: For a new refused verdict, does “otherwise false and the current Activation is the one returned” require returning the existing current Activation, or must the returned activation be None as the RETURN_SHAPE requires?

quotes: a new verdict sets activate true in its change exactly when it is admitted and the implementation is not that current activation, otherwise false and the current Activation is the one returned
MUST return a SubmissionResult with the implementation, the new or reused verdict, and when admitted the current Activation, new or existing, otherwise None.
judgement.why: The FIELD_ASSIGNMENT returns the current Activation for the otherwise case, which includes a new refused verdict, while RETURN_SHAPE requires None when the verdict is not admitted.

topics.topic: Define the representation and encoding used when comparing canonical_bytes with guard_value in the prove_version phase 4 guard rule
questions: Must canonical_bytes return canonical JSON text instead of bytes, or must the guard rule specify decoding its bytes (or encoding guard_value) before comparison?

quotes: guard_value is canonical JSON text, and it is a member when it equals, as text, the canonical JSON (canonical_bytes) of one enum member or of the const.
judgement.why: The function returns bytes, while the guard rule requires a text-to-text comparison without specifying any conversion.

topics.topic: How to record an empty mapped value output and its empty-list NodeExecution
questions: Must an empty mapped value output be written beforehand in a RecordRunProgressChange with no executions, or in the same change as the empty-list NodeExecution?

quotes: Every StoredValue runs derives for delivery — the list element a mapped element receives, and a mapped node's value list when first delivered — MUST be written with record_change in a RecordRunProgressChange with no executions, status running and the run's waiting points and outputs unchanged before fit_port_value checks it and before execute_function_element or reach_operation_element receives it: read_value_bytes, and every module below runs, reads only a StoredValue that is written.

A mapped node over an empty list executes and sends nothing and writes one NodeExecution succeeded without map_index, executed naming its pinned implementation or binding, every output an empty list of the empty list's class: a value output a StoredValuesRef to the StoredValue of [] published with put_value_bytes and written in the same change, a file output an empty SpooledFilesRef; a mapped node concludes only when every element concluded, succeeded only when all succeeded.
judgement.divergence: One implementation first writes the empty-list StoredValue in a separate RecordRunProgressChange containing no executions and later records the NodeExecution; another writes the StoredValue and empty-list NodeExecution together in one change. Store observers and recovery logic notice the different persisted change sequence.
judgement.why: The general prerequisite requires a separate no-executions change, while the empty-list rule requires the value to be written in the same change as its NodeExecution.
